additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states 'מַחֲזִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִינַת מָה וְאֶפֶס וָאַיִן.' The word מה (what? / nothingness) is used here in the kabbalistic sense of self-nullification — the state of a leader who holds himself as nothing. This follows the standard Breslov usage where מה echoes Moses's 'וְנַחְנוּ מָה' (Shemot 16:7 — 'and we are what?') as the paradigm of humble leadership. In this Torah, מה is the central node of the humility cluster. It connects to אפס and אין as parallel expressions of the same state (bechina), and to the kabbalistic identity אֲחוֹרַיִם דְּמ"ה (the back-of-MaH from Etz Chaim) which is its gematria anchor. This node is not in the dataset for Torah #95.

additions.reason: The kabbalistic term from Etz Chaim (Sha'ar Arich Anpin, ch. 12): 'אֲחוֹרַיִם דְּמ"ה' — the back-aspect/posterior of MaH. In the Lurianic framework, the 'back' (אחוריים) of a sefira or divine name represents its reduced/contracted light that faces outward and downward rather than upward and inward. The back-of-MaH is gematria-equivalent to פה: אחוריים מ"ה = מ (40) + ה (5) = 45 total, but remove מה (=45) from אחוריים-דמ"ה, the remaining letters spell פ"ה. The Rebbe uses this as the interpretive key: the 'basket' is the acharayim of MaH, and removing MaH leaves only the mouth of public disgrace. This concept is NOT currently in the dataset for Torah #95 and needs to be added.

additions.reason: When מה is removed from the leader's self-understanding, what remains is פה. The Rebbe explains this via the Etz Chaim formula: 'אֲחוֹרַיִם דְּמ"ה, תָּסִיר מ"ה נִשְׁאָר פ"ה.' The פה is not merely the consequence of arrogance; it IS the nature of the arrogant state when viewed from the outside. The word הַיְנוּ (meaning / that is) establishes the bechina: 'אֲזַי נִשְׁאָר פֶּה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם פּוֹתְחִים אֶת פִּיהֶם' — 'then PeH remains, MEANING people open their mouths.' The peh is the public aspect of the arrogant leader's reality. This is the evil mirror-concept of מה: where מה is the humility-state (no mouth, just being), פה is the arrogance-state (all mouth, public disgrace). This node is not in the dataset for Torah #95.

additions.reason: Arrogance (גאוה) is the opposite pole to self-nullification (מה). The Rebbe's teaching explicitly contrasts: 'מַחֲזִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִינַת מָה' vs. 'שֶׁאֵין מַחֲזִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְמָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא מִתְגָּאֶה.' The arrogant leader is the evil mirror of Package 1's humble leader. When the basket is removed and מה is stripped away, the resulting state is גאוה — and גאוה IS פה, because the Rebbe equates them via the formula. Arrogance and the opened mouth against the leader are parallel expressions of the same evil reality (the absence of מה). This node is not in the dataset for Torah #95.

So בזיון and פה are bechinas of each other: both are aspects of the same reality (what happens to the arrogant leader). Biz'ayon is not caused by the peh; biz'ayon IS the peh in action. They are instruments in the eitza chain, not co-essential concepts.

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_summary: Package 1 (מה/אפס/אין — humility/self-nullification) is the good pole. Package 3 (גאוה/פה/בזיון — arrogance/mouth/disgrace) is the evil mirror. Package 2 (קופה של שרצים / אחוריים דמ"ה — the humbling mechanism) is the neutral structural bridge between them. The eitza flow is: Package 2 → Package 1 (the basket CAUSES humility) and [absence of Package 2] → Package 3 (without the basket, arrogance and disgrace follow). This matches the Torah's structure perfectly.
